properties.natural_language: Before any memory operation (mstore/mstore8/mload/mcopy), the stack MUST contain the required number of operands: position for mload/mstore8, position+value for mstore, src+dst+length for mcopy.
After memory expansion, all newly allocated bytes MUST be initialized to zero, ensuring no data leakage from previous allocations.
Memory size MUST only grow monotonically during a single execution frame; it MUST never shrink.
When mcopy is invoked with overlapping source and destination ranges, the implementation MUST read all source bytes before writing to the destination, behaving like memmove rather than memcpy.
Memory expansion MUST be implicitly bounded by gas costs; any attempt to allocate memory beyond what the available gas can cover MUST result in an out-of-gas exception.
The memory_write and memory_read_bytes functions MUST correctly handle zero-length operations as no-ops without side effects.
After a memory write operation completes, the written data MUST be exactly retrievable by a subsequent read at the same position and length.
Before gas charging for memory operations, the gas calculation MUST include both the base opcode cost and the quadratic memory expansion cost.
After mcopy gas calculation, the total gas MUST include GAS_COPY * ceil32(length)/32 in addition to base and expansion costs.
Stack values used as memory positions MUST be valid U256 integers representable as memory offsets without causing integer overflow in position calculations.

Before receiving SSZ-encoded ProgressiveContainer data via P2P gossip, the serialized data length MUST be validated against application-defined runtime limits before full deserialization to prevent DoS via oversized payloads.

Before processing SSZ containers received from P2P gossip, the container structure MUST be validated per EIP-7688 ProgressiveContainer rules including correct active_fields bitmask and stable generalized indices.

Before accepting a merkle proof from an off-chain verifier, the proof's generalized index MUST be validated to correspond to a known field in the ProgressiveContainer schema, and inactive fields MUST NOT produce valid proofs.

Before an on-chain smart contract verifies an SSZ merkle proof, the generalized indices used MUST remain stable across fork transitions per EIP-7688, and malformed proof inputs MUST NOT cause EVM execution anomalies.

Before a hardware wallet signs an SSZ container, the container format MUST match the expected EIP-7688 ProgressiveContainer structure, and signed data MUST match the expected container hash to prevent signing incompatibility across migrations.
After converting a legacy Container to ProgressiveContainer, the active_fields bitmask MUST have exactly one bit set to 1 for each existing field, ensuring all current fields remain accessible.
After appending a new field to a ProgressiveContainer, the generalized indices of all pre-existing fields MUST remain unchanged.
After removing a field from a ProgressiveContainer by setting its active_fields bit to 0, the generalized index for that field MUST remain reserved and MUST NOT be reused for new fields.
After rejecting data that exceeds ProgressiveList length limits, the system MUST NOT have performed any partial deserialization or state mutation from the rejected data.
After successful merkle proof verification, the computed root MUST match the expected state root exactly; any mismatch MUST result in proof rejection.
The generalized index for any field in a ProgressiveContainer MUST remain stable across all fork transitions, regardless of field additions or removals.
ProgressiveContainer serialization format MUST mirror legacy Container serialization for backward compatibility with existing tools.
Application-defined runtime limits for ProgressiveList length MUST be enforced consistently to prevent memory exhaustion from unbounded lists.
During the transition period, verifiers MUST support both legacy merkleization and ProgressiveContainer merkleization to maintain backward compatibility.
Migration to ProgressiveContainer MUST occur at or before the first fork where any structural change would break existing merkle proofs.
SSZ MUST remain Ethereum's serialization standard; any migration away from SSZ would require re-evaluation of the ProgressiveContainer approach.
Incremental construction of Validator entries in ProgressiveList MUST process entries one at a time to maintain consistency.
Before executing a CREATE opcode, the caller MUST have sufficient balance for the endowment, the nonce MUST not exceed 2^64-1, and the call stack depth MUST be less than 1024.
After successful contract creation via CREATE/CREATE2, the new contract address MUST be pushed to the stack; after failure, zero MUST be pushed.
The CREATE2 address computation MUST be deterministic: given the same sender, salt, and init_code_hash, the resulting address MUST always be identical.
Before executing any CALL variant, the call stack depth MUST be verified to be within the 1024 limit to prevent stack overflow attacks.
At most 63/64 of the remaining gas MUST be forwarded to child calls; the parent MUST retain at least 1/64 of gas.
After a child call reverts, all state changes from the child MUST be rolled back, but the return data buffer MUST still be populated with the revert reason data.
When CALLCODE or DELEGATECALL targets an empty account (no code), execution MUST succeed immediately with no state changes.
SELFDESTRUCT in Prague MUST only mark for deletion contracts that were created within the same transaction (EIP-6780). Pre-existing contracts MUST only have their balance transferred.
After SELFDESTRUCT executes, the contract's entire remaining balance MUST be transferred to the beneficiary, and execution MUST halt immediately.
After RETURN executes, the output data from the specified memory region MUST be stored in the EVM output and made available to the caller.
After REVERT executes, the output data MUST be available to the caller AND all state changes in the current frame MUST be rolled back.
An attacker MUST NOT be able to predict nonces to front-run CREATE and deploy malicious code at expected addresses, as nonces are incremented atomically.
After warm/cold access determination, warm addresses MUST be charged GAS_WARM_ACCESS (100) and cold addresses MUST be charged GAS_COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS (2600).

Before a wallet extension injects a provider into window.evmproviders, it MUST check if the namespace already exists and create it only if absent, to prevent race conditions with concurrent extensions.
Before registering a wallet provider, the provider object MUST be validated: key format MUST match [a-z0-9_]+, UUID MUST be valid UUIDv4, and the provider MUST implement the EIP-1193 interface.
Before rendering a wallet provider's SVG icon, the icon data MUST be validated as data:image/svg+xml;base64 format and MUST be rendered within an tag to prevent XSS via embedded JavaScript in SVG.
Before a DApp user selects a wallet provider, the DApp MUST NOT be able to override the user's preference or inject fake providers into the selection UI.
The window.evmproviders object MUST be protected via Object.freeze after registration to prevent runtime tampering with the provider list.
A wallet provider's UUID MUST be consistent across all versions of the same wallet product but MUST be distinct from UUIDs of other wallet products.

Wallet extensions MUST be assumed to be intentionally installed by the user; however, the system MUST still validate provider objects to mitigate the risk of malicious extensions injecting fake providers.
DApps SHOULD handle non-conforming provider keys gracefully since snake_case naming is only recommended, not mandatory.
Wallet extensions MUST inject providers before DApp code attempts to enumerate them; late injection could cause wallets to be missed.
All EIP-1193 security considerations MUST apply to interactions with discovered wallet providers.
After rendering an SVG icon in an tag, any embedded JavaScript in the SVG MUST NOT execute, ensuring XSS prevention.
The EMPTY_ACCOUNT constant (nonce=0, balance=0, code=empty) MUST be used consistently across all code paths to represent non-existent accounts.
After RLP encoding an account, the encoded bytes MUST deterministically represent [nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash] such that no two different valid accounts produce the same encoding.
Before encoding an account for trie storage, the storage root MUST be computed separately from the account storage trie and passed to the encode function.
Before submitting blob data for commitment, the blob submitter MUST provide valid data that can generate a correct KZG commitment.
Before accepting a VersionedHash, the version byte (first byte of Hash32) MUST be validated as 0x01 for the current blob version, and the remaining 31 bytes MUST be a valid hash.
The Bytes, Uint, U256, and Hash32 types from ethereum base modules MUST correctly handle all edge cases including boundary values to prevent overflow or underflow.
The return data buffer MUST be isolated per call frame and MUST NOT be accessible across different execution contexts.
Before executing a call-like opcode (CALL, DELEGATECALL, CREATE, etc.), the return data buffer MUST be cleared to prevent data leakage from previous calls.
Before RETURNDATACOPY executes, the bounds check MUST verify that offset + length <= RETURNDATASIZE with no integer overflow; violation MUST trigger an out-of-gas exception.
Reading zero bytes from the return data buffer at offset == RETURNDATASIZE MUST succeed as a valid empty read at the boundary.
After a subcall completes (success or failure), the return data buffer MUST be populated with the complete return/revert data from the called contract.
A called contract MUST NOT be able to manipulate the caller's return data buffer except through the normal RETURN/REVERT mechanisms.
After RETURNDATASIZE executes, the value pushed to the stack MUST exactly equal the number of bytes in the current return data buffer, consuming exactly 2 gas.
After successful RETURNDATACOPY, the specified bytes MUST be copied from the return data buffer to EVM memory at the destination offset, consuming 3 + 3*ceil(length/32) gas.
Before processing a block received from the beacon chain via Engine API, the execution layer MUST validate JWT authentication on the Engine API channel.
Before accepting a block from a block producer via P2P, the execution layer MUST perform full block validation including header validity, transaction list integrity, and state root verification.
Before accepting a block as valid in Paris, the difficulty field MUST equal zero, the nonce field MUST be all zeros, and the ommers hash MUST equal EMPTY_OMMER_HASH.
After applying the block body, the computed state root, transaction root, receipt root, and logs bloom MUST exactly match the values claimed in the block header.
In Paris (post-merge), every block MUST have zero difficulty, zero nonce, and empty ommers. Non-zero values in any of these fields MUST cause block rejection.
Before accepting an EIP-1559 transaction, max_fee_per_gas MUST be >= max_priority_fee_per_gas, and the sender's balance MUST cover gas * max_fee_per_gas + value.
Before processing a transaction, the sender address MUST be recovered from the ECDSA signature, and the sender MUST be an externally-owned account (not a contract).
After transaction execution, the gas refund MUST be capped at 20% of gas consumed, and the priority fee MUST be paid to the coinbase address.
The EIP-1559 base fee MUST adjust by at most 12.5% per block (1/BASE_FEE_MAX_CHANGE_DENOMINATOR) and MUST never become negative.
The Engine API between consensus and execution layers MUST use JWT authentication and MUST be reliable and timely for block processing.
The EMPTY_OMMER_HASH MUST equal keccak256(RLP([])) = 0x1dcc4de8dec75d7aab85b567b6ccd41ad312451b948a7413f0a142fd40d49347.
The beacon chain consensus layer MUST correctly validate blocks before passing execution payloads to the EL; a sufficient number of validators MUST be honest.
After the base fee validation, the computed base fee MUST match the block header's base_fee_per_gas exactly, or the block MUST be rejected.
Before executing SLOAD in Istanbul, the gas cost MUST be 800 (increased from 200 pre-Istanbul) to reflect actual trie access costs.
Before executing BALANCE in Istanbul, the gas cost MUST be 700 (increased from 400 pre-Istanbul).
Istanbul SLOAD gas pricing (800) MUST apply uniformly to all storage accesses without warm/cold distinction (warm/cold comes in Berlin fork).
After SELFBALANCE (0x47) executes, the contract's own balance MUST be pushed to the stack for exactly 5 gas, providing a cheaper alternative to BALANCE for self-queries.
The CHAINID opcode MUST return the correct canonical EIP-155 chain ID for the executing network to ensure cross-chain replay protection.
After a contract validates CHAINID against the expected chain, a mismatch MUST be detectable so the contract can revert to prevent cross-chain replay.
Before executing the BLAKE2b precompile at address 0x09, the input MUST be validated as exactly 213 bytes with correct format; invalid input MUST cause the call to fail.
The BLAKE2b precompile implementation MUST be constant-time to prevent timing side-channel attacks that could leak information about inputs.
After BLAKE2b precompile execution, the gas consumed MUST equal rounds * 1, where rounds is extracted from the first 4 bytes of the 213-byte input.
Existing contracts relying on SLOAD costing 200 gas may fail or become more expensive after Istanbul; this is an accepted breaking change.
Before processing a block from a block producer, the block header MUST pass all validation checks including gas limits, base fee, timestamps, difficulty=0, nonce=0, and parent hash consistency.

Before accepting a transaction via JSON-RPC, the transaction MUST pass full validation: gas availability, sender recovery via ECDSA, nonce match, EIP-1559 fee constraints, blob hash validation, balance sufficiency, and sender EOA verification.
Before accepting a blob transaction (Type 3), the blob gas consumption MUST NOT exceed MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK (1,179,648), and all blob versioned hashes MUST use KZG version 0x01.
After block body execution, the computed state root, transaction root, receipt root, and gas used MUST exactly match the block header claims, or the block MUST be rejected.
After transaction execution, the gas refund MUST be computed as min(gas_used_before_refund/5, refund_counter), and the EIP-7623 floor MUST be applied as max(gas_after_refund, calldata_floor_cost).
The BEACON_ROOTS_ADDRESS and HISTORY_STORAGE_ADDRESS system contracts MUST be correctly deployed and immutable; missing code MUST cause block validation failure.
Signature recovery using secp256k1_recover MUST be deterministic and correctly implemented; incorrect recovery would lead to unauthorized fund transfers.
SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_GAS (30,000,000) MUST be sufficient for all system contract operations (beacon roots, history storage).
Attackers MUST NOT be able to forge valid ECDSA signatures without knowing the private key; the secp256k1 curve assumption underlies all transaction security.
The 'valid delegation code' check for sender validation MUST follow EIP-7702 format with proper authorization chain.
The rolling 255-block window for block hash access MUST maintain exactly 255 most recent block hashes, returning empty for requests beyond the window.
Unchecked system transactions that fail MUST silently revert their state changes without propagating errors to block processing.
After processing all transactions and requests, deposit requests MUST be parsed from logs, withdrawal requests MUST be retrieved from the predeploy, and all requests MUST be ordered by type.
After processing beacon chain withdrawals, validator balances MUST be increased by the withdrawal amount multiplied by 10^9 (Gwei to Wei conversion).
After gas and fee calculation, the gas limit change from parent block MUST be within parent_gas_limit/1024 (GAS_LIMIT_ADJUSTMENT_FACTOR).

Before decoding a transaction, the first byte MUST be inspected to determine type: >= 0xc0 for legacy, 0x01 for access list, 0x02 for fee market, 0x03 for blob, 0x04 for SetCode. Unknown types MUST be rejected.
Before accepting a transaction, intrinsic gas MUST be computed as TX_BASE_COST (21000) + calldata cost + create cost + access list cost + auth cost, and MUST meet gas sufficiency.
Before signature validation, the R component MUST be in range (0, SECP256K1N) and the S component MUST be in range (0, SECP256K1N/2] to prevent signature malleability.
After successful sender recovery, the derived address MUST be the keccak256 hash of the recovered public key with the rightmost 20 bytes extracted.
RLP decoding MUST correctly reject all malformed transaction data to prevent parsing errors or incorrect field extraction.
The SECP256K1N constant and secp256k1 curve parameters MUST be correctly implemented to ensure signature validation accuracy.
Before contract creation transactions, the init code size MUST NOT exceed MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE (EIP-3860) to prevent DoS via oversized deployment code.
Before accepting a transaction, the nonce MUST be less than 2^64-1 per EIP-2681 to prevent nonce overflow.
In calldata cost calculation, each byte is counted as a 'token': zero bytes cost 0 gas and non-zero bytes cost STANDARD_CALLDATA_TOKEN_COST (4 gas).
For SetCodeTransaction (Type 4/EIP-7702), the authorization cost MUST follow EIP-7702 specification for per-empty-account charges.
After signature hash computation for legacy transactions with chain_id (EIP-155), the hash MUST include the chain_id to provide replay protection across different chains.
After EIP-7623 floor gas calculation, the floor cost MUST equal (total_tokens * FLOOR_CALLDATA_COST) + TX_BASE_COST, ensuring minimum gas for calldata-heavy transactions.
Before accepting any block or transaction from a peer node via devp2p, the data MUST be fully validated. Eclipse attack mitigations and peer reputation scoring MUST be in place.
All blocks received via P2P from peer nodes MUST undergo full validation including header, transaction list, and state transition verification before acceptance.
Before accepting block proposals from a beacon chain validator via P2P gossip, the proposer signature, slot assignment, and attestation validity MUST be verified.
Duplicate or conflicting attestations from validators MUST be rejected, and slashing conditions MUST be enforced.
Before accepting block bids from MEV-Boost relays, the relay-provided execution payloads MUST pass full EL validation. Censorship resistance mechanisms SHOULD be considered.
Block bids from MEV relays MUST be validated for correctness before inclusion; invalid relay data MUST NOT affect node consensus state.
